raw.title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
raw.body: Distributed learning in embodied reinforcement-learning agents offers a degree of privacy by retaining raw sensor data on-device and transmitting only policy gradients to the server. Yet temporal structure can amplify this leakage beyond single-frame attacks. We introduce Temporal Reconstruction Attack on Consecutive Encodings (TRACE), an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack that autoregressively reconstructs the sequence of private observation-action trajectories from per-step policy-learning gradients. The attack exploits two structural signals ignored by prior single-frame methods: (i) cross-time correlation between successive embodied gradients, which we formalize via a conditional mutual-information bound, and (ii) closed-form action recovery from policy-head gradient structure, which we prove exact when standard entropy regularization is sufficiently small. On held-out embodied scenes, TRACE reaches $18.8$ dB PSNR with near-perfect action recovery at $3$-$4.5$ ms per reconstructed frame, dominating the learning-based baseline across all reconstruction metrics and exceeding optimization attacks while running orders of magnitude faster. Further evaluation demonstrates TRACE's broader applicability across recurrent, residual, and compact transformer victim architectures, multi-modal inputs, and larger discrete action spaces. Defense experiments suggest that protecting temporal gradient streams may require sequence-aware privacy mechanisms.

concepts: AI 안전 및 비밀 과제 회피

key_points.point: TRACE는 연속 정책 그래디언트의 시간적 상관성과 정책 헤드 그래디언트 구조를 이용해 관측‑행동 궤적을 자동회귀적으로 복원한다.
복원 품질은 18.8 dB PSNR, 행동 복원은 거의 완벽하며 프레임당 3‑4.5 ms로 기존 방법보다 빠르고 정확하다.
실험은 순환, 잔차, 경량 트랜스포머 등 다양한 아키텍처에 적용 가능함을 보여주며, 시퀀스‑인식 프라이버시 방어가 필요함을 시사한다.

analysis.positioning: 분산된 embodied RL에서 원시 센서 데이터를 디바이스에 보관하고 정책 그래디언트만 전송하는 방식은 프라이버시를 제공한다고 여겨졌지만, 기존 단일 프레임 공격만 고려했다. 본 논문은 시간적 그래디언트의 상관성을 이용해 연속 관측‑행동 궤적을 복원하는 TRACE 공격을 제안하며, 기존 방법보다 빠르고 정확하게 프라이버시 침해 가능성을 보여준다.
production_ideas: 연속 그래디언트의 시간적 상관성을 활용해 연합 학습 중 언어 모델 업데이트에서 개인 텍스트 유출을 탐지한다.
정책 헤드 그래디언트 구조의 폐쇄형 복원을 이용해 온‑디바이스 음성 인식 모델의 사용자 입력을 복원, 감사 도구로 활용한다.
TRACE의 amortized inversion 방식을 시계열 예측 모델(예: 주가 예측) 업데이트에 적용해 과거 민감 데이터가 얼마나 추론될 수 있는지 평가한다.

quiz.question: TRACE가 최적화 기반 공격보다 빠르게 복원할 수 있는 주요 이유는 무엇인가?
options: 폐쇄형 행동 복원과 자동회귀 추론을 사용한다
quiz.explanation: TRACE는 정책 헤드 그래디언트에서 행동을 정확히 복원하는 폐쇄형 식과, 이전 프레임 정보를 이용한 자동회귀 복원 과정을 사용해 반복적인 최적화 과정을 생략하므로 속도가 크게 향상된다.

quiz.question: TRACE에서 사용된 조건부 상호정보(bound)의 역할은 무엇인가?
options: 연속 그래디언트 간에 공유되는 정보를 정량화한다
quiz.explanation: 조건부 상호정보 bound는 인접한 시간 단계의 그래디언트가 서로 얼마나 의존하는지를 정량화해, 시간적 상관성을 이용한 복원의 이론적 근거를 제공한다.

# The Provenance Tax: Understanding the Impact of LLM Watermarking on AI Agent Behavior

![Andrea Siposova](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/677e57d57f0aaef07252db12/6983079e7e6962fdcedc80b6_profile_picture.avif)

Andrea Siposova

September 17, 2026

4

min read

![The Provenance Tax: Understanding the Impact of LLM Watermarking on AI Agent Behavior](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/677e57d57f0aaef07252db12/6aab8f3234c02c13abcd8f76_The%20Impact%20of%20%20LLM%20Watermarking%20%20on%20Agent%20Security%20%26%20Safety%20-%20744.png)

## On this page

[This is a h2](#)

[This is a h3](#)

[This is a h4](#)

Recently, [Anthropic announced that future Claude models would embed an invisible watermark](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-text-watermark) in their output [1], [2], and subsequently disclosed that the watermark is based on Google DeepMind’s [SynthID-Text](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08025-4) [2], [3]. Text watermarking itself is not new, but its deployment now has regulatory relevance. [Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/50/) [4] requires providers of AI systems generating synthetic text to mark their outputs in a machine-readable format and make them detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, using technical solutions that are effective, interoperable, robust, and reliable as far as technically feasible.

‍

Watermarking is designed for provenance, but SynthID-Text changes the process by which the model generates each next token. At the model level, this can change safety behavior, including whether the model refuses a harmful request and whether that refusal holds under prompt injection. At the agent level, the same sampled tokens can determine which tool is called and what arguments are passed to it. **Prompt injection connects these two settings because a weakened refusal becomes more consequential when the model can also act through tools.** Such a watermarking procedure can therefore affect both what the model says and what an agent does. We call this behavioral effect **sampling drift.**

‍

Whether this drift appears in practice is an empirical question. We find that it does, in both model refusal behavior and agent tool calling. The effect is model- and key-dependent and can be obscured by aggregate scores when changes in opposite directions cancel. We therefore report both net performance and paired disagreement between watermarked and unwatermarked runs. Further, the closing section discusses what it means for AI safety and security and what developers should do about it.

‍

## **Built for Content Provenance, Deployed Inside Agents**

‍

A text watermark embeds a signal that allows output to be identified as AI-generated. Existing approaches include post-processing methods and methods integrated directly into LLM generation [8]. Generation-time approaches include logits-biasing methods [5], distortion-free keyed sampling [6], cryptographically motivated constructions [7], and SynthID-Text’s Tournament sampling [3]. Figure 1 contrasts this process with ordinary sampling. We use SynthID’s non-distortionary configuration, which preserves the original token distribution in expectation over the watermark randomness while individual generations under a fixed key can still differ [3]. Dathathri et al. report no measurable quality degradation across nearly twenty million Gemini responses [3].

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/677e57d57f0aaef07252db12/6aab907c2750694e8b5ffc13_56a33d01.png)

**Figure 1. Standard versus watermarked text generation.** Ordinary generation samples from the model’s token distribution. A generative watermark adds a random seed generator, sampling algorithm, and scoring function; SynthID-Text uses tournament sampling. Adapted from Dathathri et al. [3].

‍

‍

Anthropic’s deployment also illustrates why this matters beyond first-party chat interfaces. The company states that watermarking is applied at the model level and covers supported models accessed through the Claude Platform API as well as cloud providers [1]. A developer using a watermarked model as the reasoning component of an agent can therefore receive watermarked outputs even when the agent itself is a separate application. This makes model-level behavioral effects of watermarking relevant to the agents built around such models.

‍

### **Same Tokens the Watermark Biases, Same Tokens the Agent Acts On**

‍

Tournament sampling has more opportunity to alter token selection where the model is uncertain. In structured output such as JSON, braces, keys, and function names are often highly predictable, while values such as queries, numbers, paths, and recipients are less so. A change that would amount to a lexical variation in ordinary prose can therefore alter an argument that an agent executes.

‍

The weights and prompt remain unchanged, but token selection does not. Importantly, non-distortionary does no

analysis.one_line_summary: 워터마크가 에이전트 행동을 바꿔 안전 검증 필요
concepts: AI 안전 및 비밀 과제 회피

key_points.point: SynthID-Text 기반 워터마크는 토큰 샘플링 방식을 바꾸어 모델의 거부 행동과 툴 호출에 ‘샘플링 드리프트’를 일으킨다.
실험 결과, 드리프트는 모델과 키에 따라 다르게 나타나며, 반대 방향 변화가 합산될 경우 전체 점수에서 가려질 수 있다.
이 현상은 AI 안전에 영향을 미치므로 개발자는 워터마크 적용 시 행동 변화를 모니터링하고 완화 방안을 설계해야 한다.

production_ideas: 코드 생성 LLM에 tournament sampling 워터마크를 적용해 AI‑generated 코드를 식별하면서 품질 저하를 최소화한다.
워터마크 적용·미적용 모델 간의 샘플링 차이를 모니터링 지표로 활용해 프로덕션 LLM 서비스에서 비정상 행동 변화를 실시간 감지한다.
툴 호출을 수행하는 자동 에이전트에 워터마크 인식을 결합해, 워터마크가 감지될 때 거부 정책을 강화해 프롬프트 인젝션 위험을 감소시킨다.

quiz.question: 본문에서 ‘샘플링 드리프트’가 의미하는 것은 무엇인가?
options: 워터마크가 토큰 확률 분포를 바꿔 모델 출력이 달라지는 현상
생성 후 텍스트에 무작위 노이즈를 추가하는 과정
하드웨어 지연으로 인한 응답 시간 변화
quiz.explanation: 워터마크는 토큰 샘플링 과정을 변경해 동일 입력에서도 다른 토큰이 선택될 수 있어 모델의 거부 및 툴 호출 행동이 달라지는 현상을 ‘샘플링 드리프트’라 부른다.

quiz.question: 왜 프롬프트 인젝션이 워터마크가 적용된 모델에서 더 큰 영향을 미치는가?
options: 워터마크가 거부 강도를 약화시켜 툴 호출까지 영향을 주기 때문
워터마크가 모든 안전 검사를 제거하기 때문
프롬프트 인젝션이 토큰 샘플링을 무시하기 때문
워터마크가 모델 속도를 높여 공격을 빠르게 수행하게 하기 때문
quiz.explanation: 워터마크가 거부 행동을 약화시키면, 프롬프트 인젝션으로 모델이 툴을 호출하도록 유도했을 때 그 영향이 확대돼 안전 위험이 커진다.

[17:31] You can you can run this for infinite number of steps, apply infinite number of iterations without adding another layer.
[17:38] And if I understand correctly, at the moment, these episodes are ephemeral.
[17:42] So they're isolated from each other.

[17:45] Like what would did you experiment with that, like they they had knowledge of what's happened before, or they could have a shared memory or something?

[17:57] Um, I think there are some more fundamental problem formulation problem we have to address.
[18:04] You know, currently we frame the problem is a stateless optimization problem.

raw.body:
Weco let an AI coding agent rewrite the harness around another agent for eight days: its code, prompts and tools, while the underlying language model stayed fixed. Tim Scarfe asks Weco co-founder Zhengyao Jiang what the reported gains over two years of human engineering actually demonstrate.

The discussion examines AIDE 85's generated code, held-out evaluation and the difficulty of separating useful discoveries from reward hacking. Jiang explains Weco's four levels of recursive self-improvement and compares the experiment with AlphaEvolve and the Darwin Gödel Machine.

The limits matter as much as the gains. Jiang explains why the experiment did not establish that the system had become a better improver. The conversation closes with open-ended search, human-designed primitives and Parameter Golf: where does the next useful idea come from when the agent is searching inside a space that people designed?

[00:19] So, I, I just said, let's stop giving them that medicine. So that means you change a variable, um, in, in, um, causal model that says do operator. So, you do this, give the patient this medicine, rather than observe the patient is taking that medicine.
[00:35] And those are two entirely different things.
[00:38] But if I just decide that they're gonna get this, uh, then I just know nothing about the disease.
raw.body:
Frank Hutter, co-founder and CEO of Prior Labs, on why a model that predicts perfectly can still point you to the wrong decision. If patients who get a medicine tend to have a disease, stopping the medicine will not cure it. Observing is not the same as intervening, and that difference is what causal machine learning is for.

From our conversation with Frank on TabPFN and foundation models for tabular data.

# [Allan's Blog](http://allanrbo.blogspot.com/)

Allan Riordan Boll's blog

## Friday, September 25, 2026

### A Jev-like wrapper for LLMs, including vision models

[![](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgslbgarcdEUUkIJWtO6Hzy1tHhrkARR5gWxsFPfsPk02zgLqPXsCoxkEIHa4ymkDB3aF-21KS9F0f4ScH9KVz-iN9GJ6yyTDC4rh8AaPG2QiCbZXDUNkRnRYLl8YDcuC8FsX9mkm-A9sb5s9V86UyC3A_I1Ai19idZYTgW1g8ZBLvwYirK97hZSw/s1600/webcam.jpeg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgslbgarcdEUUkIJWtO6Hzy1tHhrkARR5gWxsFPfsPk02zgLqPXsCoxkEIHa4ymkDB3aF-21KS9F0f4ScH9KVz-iN9GJ6yyTDC4rh8AaPG2QiCbZXDUNkRnRYLl8YDcuC8FsX9mkm-A9sb5s9V86UyC3A_I1Ai19idZYTgW1g8ZBLvwYirK97hZSw/s1369/webcam.jpeg)

I was intrigued by [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) and the self-hostable projects appearing around it, such as [OpenJev](https://huggingface.co/openjev/openjev) and [SemIf](https://github.com/TheoLeeCJ/SemIf-OpenJev). Reading about them introduced me to a neat trick: reading an LLM's token probabilities.

Apparently this is an old trick for some people. See e.g. [OpenAI's logprobs cookbook](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/using_logprobs). But it was new to me.

I believe the basic idea is to write a prompt like this:

```
State: My order arrived broken and I want a refund.
Question: Which team should handle this?
[A] billing
[B] shipping
[C] returns
Answer with the letter of the best option only.
```

Then add a few JSON request parameters to a compatible Chat Completions request:

```
{
  "max_completion_tokens": 1,
  "logprobs": true,
  "top_logprobs": 20
}
```

The LLM API will return the letter plus the model's log probabilities for alternative tokens.

Repeat for each question. Forcing it to generating only one token avoids a lengthy answer and is super quick, though processing the input still costs time. Though for each of the questions a shared state prefix can be KV-cached if the backend supports it.

The fun part: this works with vision models too. Jev's [documented request format](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart) currently describes only text/JSON state. I added an `attachments` field for images for my local experiments.

My example captures webcam frames, sends base64 JPEGs, and prints a table: is a person visible, are we indoors or outdoors, and how bright is the scene? With Gemma 4 12B on my RTX 3090, I get around **1 frames per second**, with three questions per frame. I also ran it against OpenAI gpt-6-luna and got around 0.2 FPS. Presumably because I didn't make any effort to avoid the cost of a separate connection through their system per question per frame.

Specialized computer vision models surely are much more efficient, but what I like here is the flexibility: change a condition by describing it in plain text.

Here's the standalone Python example (OpenCV is just used for convenient access to the webcam, not for any actual computer vision):

```

# /// script
# dependencies = ["opencv-python"]
# ///

uv run webcam.py
uv run webcam.py https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-6-luna
OpenAI reads OPENAI_API_KEY.
